rationale: Classic post-earnings-announcement-drift event study (Foster, Olsen, Shevlin 1984, The Accounting Review). Explicit sample selection (Section 3: 1982 Compustat quarterly tape, 2,454 companies -> 2,213 after 10-consecutive-earnings screen -> 2,053 with CRSP daily data; quarterly earnings file Q2 1970 to Q4 1981; CAR sample 1974Q1-1981Q4, 32 quarters, over 56,000 observations). Fully operationalized methodology: four unexpected-earnings models with exact formulas (eqs. 8-13), abnormal-return estimation via NYSE size-decile companion portfolios (eq. 15) and via the equally-weighted market (eq. 17), simulation-based significance testing (1,000 trials of 8,000 random firm-quarters), and cross-sectional regressions of portfolio CARs on forecast-error-portfolio and size-quintile codings (eq. 16). Nine tables of numerical results (Tables 1-9) covering portfolio transition frequencies, forecast-error medians, NYSE size-decile returns/betas, pooled CARs across windows [-1,0]/[-60,0]/[+1,+60], subperiod counts, size-quintile CAR breakdowns, regression coefficients/R-squares, and robustness under market-adjusted returns. Data sources (Compustat quarterly earnings + announcement dates; CRSP daily returns/prices/shares) are standard and expected to be in ClickHouse.
